blocks.text: An input record contains id|priority|done|title. The ID is a positive representable int, unique within the candidate dataset. Priority is one through three. Completion is zero or one. Numeric fields require whole-field conversion: a leading plus sign, surrounding whitespace, or trailing characters is rejected by this grammar. Leading zeros are accepted. Negative numeric syntax may parse, but negative values fail the relevant domain checks.

blocks.text: Titles contain one through two hundred printable ASCII bytes, exclude vertical bars, and must include at least one non-space character. Leading and trailing ordinary spaces are retained. A broader format needs an explicit encoding and character-policy revision.

blocks.text: The default limits are ten thousand accepted rows and two hundred fifty-six retained bytes per line before LF. A trailing CR is removed for CRLF parsing, but it counts toward the line limit as delivered by the stream. The file adapter opens in binary mode. Standard input can be subject to platform text translation, so the limit concerns characters presented to the parser, not a universal physical-byte count before all platform processing.

blocks.text: An empty file is a valid empty replacement. A blank record is invalid. A final nonempty record without LF is accepted. On any returned input error, accepted tasks remain unchanged. Exceptional allocation failures also occur before publication. Input position and stream state are not restored. Rendering returns an owning string; writing can leave a prefix in an external sink on failure. The command-line adapter reports ordinary validation failures with exit two and detected operational failures with exit three. Operating-system signals and forced process termination are outside that exit-status contract.

topics.title: D.2 Inspect the public boundary
topics.summary: Task is a simple transfer value; its fields are public so snapshots are easy to inspect. The invariant belongs to the private accepted collection inside Report, which only receives validated tasks through load. Constructing an arbitrary Task in a caller does not insert it into that collection. This is a deliberate boundary: the application does not claim that every possible standalone task object is valid at every moment.

blocks.text: The API returns copied snapshots and completed text. It does not expose mutable accepted storage or iterators that survive replacement. Error objects own only a code and line number, while diagnostic strings come from fixed literals. These choices keep ownership understandable at the cost of some copying, which is appropriate for the bounded instructional workload.

topics.chapterTitle: Appendix D — A Bounded, Transactional Reporting Application
topics.title: D.3 Follow parsing, validation, and commit
topics.summary: The bounded reader retains at most the configured number of characters in its line string. It reads one additional non-newline character to detect an overlong record but does not append it. The input is not drained after rejection. This gives a concrete retained-line bound without promising a precise process-memory ceiling: string capacity, stream buffers, candidate tasks, index nodes, and rendering copies still consume storage.

blocks.text: The private candidate accumulates validated values. The only accepted-state publication is the final vector swap after clean end-of-input. A valid empty candidate deliberately replaces old state with an empty value. A failed nonempty candidate is destroyed instead. This is why “the load returned no tasks” is not enough to classify success or failure; the optional error result and the accepted-state transition must be considered together.

blocks.text: Rendering takes a filtered owning copy of unfinished tasks and sorts by priority and ID. The optional grouped header is derived from those selected tasks, not from all accepted tasks. A classic locale makes numeric presentation stable under this renderer’s policy. The write method creates the whole string before touching the caller’s sink, checks that its size fits the stream write count, and uses an unformatted write to avoid inherited field-width formatting. A sink failure can still retain a prefix.

topics.title: D.4 Keep command-line policy outside the domain
topics.summary: The adapter recognizes --grouped, --help, and at most one input file. With no file, it borrows standard input. With a file, a local stream owns the open association and remains alive through loading. The raw pointer selects one existing stream; it never owns or deletes either target.

blocks.text: The adapter reports structured validation errors with a line number and stable message. It checks final output and flushing before returning normal success. The broad final exception handler is an application boundary for unexpected standard exceptions, not a parser branch that disguises resource failure as malformed data. The core can therefore be tested independently with in-memory streams.

topics.title: D.6 Acceptance review and remaining work
topics.summary: The accepted-state guarantee is supported by a visible commit point and regression checks. The retained-line bound is supported by checking before append and exact-boundary tests. Input-consumption behavior is exposed by the failing stream buffer. Output non-atomicity is exposed by the prefix-retaining sink. These are separate pieces of evidence rather than a single vague claim that the program is “safe.”

sections.purpose: Follow the book’s subsections in order.

sections.title: D.1 Define the extension’s contract
sections.purpose: The compact Chapter 21 application is the starting point. This extension retains its task-reporting purpose while making input limits, structured failures, and publication boundaries more ex

sections.title: D.2 Inspect the public boundary
sections.purpose: Task is a simple transfer value; its fields are public so snapshots are easy to inspect. The invariant belongs to the private accepted collection inside Report, which only receives validated

sections.title: D.3 Follow parsing, validation, and commit
sections.purpose: The bounded reader retains at most the configured number of characters in its line string. It reads one additional non-newline character to detect an overlong record but does not append it.

sections.title: D.4 Keep command-line policy outside the domain
sections.purpose: The adapter recognizes --grouped, --help, and at most one input file. With no file, it borrows standard input. With a file, a local stream owns the open association and remains alive through

sections.title: D.5 Test the boundary, not just the happy path
sections.purpose: The command-line fixture file contains thirty-six cases spanning valid input, empty input, ties, CRLF, final-line policy, title limits, syntax failures, numeric domains, duplicates, file sel

sections.title: D.6 Acceptance review and remaining work
